operatorProperties.code:
def process(fireWeather) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    df = fireWeather[['start_year', 'start_day_of_year']].copy()

    # Use yearly median start day-of-year as a robust estimate of the distribution's center
    yearly = (
        df.groupby('start_year', as_index=False)
          .agg(median_start_doy=('start_day_of_year', 'median'),
               mean_start_doy=('start_day_of_year', 'mean'),
               n=('start_day_of_year', 'size'))
          .sort_values('start_year')
    )

    # Compare early vs late periods (first 1/3 years vs last 1/3 years) to detect shift direction
    years = yearly['start_year'].tolist()
    k = max(2, len(years) // 3)
    early = yearly.head(k)
    late = yearly.tail(k)

    early_median = float(early['median_start_doy'].median())
    late_median = float(late['median_start_doy'].median())
    shifted_later = late_median > early_median
    shifted_earlier = late_median < early_median

    return pd.DataFrame([{
        'early_years': f"{int(early['start_year'].min())}-{int(early['start_year'].max())}",
        'late_years': f"{int(late['start_year'].min())}-{int(late['start_year'].max())}",
        'early_median_of_yearly_medians': early_median,
        'late_median_of_yearly_medians': late_median,
        'shift_direction': 'later' if shifted_later else ('earlier' if shifted_earlier else 'no_change'),
        'shifted': bool(shifted_later or shifted_earlier)
    }])
